subject.title: Heartbeat drift fix (PR #39182) causes aggressive retry that blocks Telegram during active conversations

question: Should the narrow fix for this issue use the linked PR's fixed 60 second requests-in-flight retry policy, a different backoff, or a public configuration surface?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but the exact retry delay changes existing heartbeat responsiveness and channel contention behavior, so automation should not choose the durable product policy alone.

options.title: Accept Fixed Delay After Repair
options.body: Use the linked PR or equivalent to preserve per-target retry timing, accept a fixed 60 second requests-in-flight retry delay, and require live channel proof before merge.

options.title: Choose Backoff Or Config
options.body: Define a configurable or adaptive retry policy first, accepting extra config/docs/test surface in exchange for operator control.

options.title: Defer To Broader Redesign
options.body: Leave this narrow issue open while prioritizing non-blocking heartbeat execution or activity-based heartbeat work instead of a retry-cadence mitigation.

recommendation.title: Accept Fixed Delay After Repair
recommendation.body: Use the linked PR or equivalent to preserve per-target retry timing, accept a fixed 60 second requests-in-flight retry delay, and require live channel proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history on the heartbeat runner and the cited no-drift behavior, and is the best available owner for the retry policy tradeoff.
